name: EZX10RF
description: The EZX10RF 5010G X10 RF transceiver and Insteon scene controller from Compacta International, which turns X10 addresses into Insteon group commands: its code records, the buffer that loads and saves them, the X10 address filter and Peek and Poke.

standardCommands.name: readDeviceText
standardCommands.description: Device Text String Request: the device answers with an extended Device Text String Response (cmd1 0x03, cmd2 0x02), D1 through D14 an ASCII string, null-terminated or 14 bytes long.

standardCommands.name: setAddressMsb
standardCommands.description: Set Address MSB: sets the high byte of the address Peek and Poke use. It must be 0x00 for the addresses the notes list.

standardCommands.name: poke
standardCommands.description: Poke: writes cmd2 to the parameter RAM at the address Peek last set, then moves to the next address.

standardCommands.name: peek
standardCommands.description: Peek: sets the address to cmd2, and reads the byte there.

standardCommands.name: loadInitializationValues
standardCommands.description: EZX10RF Control, Load Initialization Values: resets the device to its factory settings.

standardCommands.name: writeCodeRecord
standardCommands.description: EZX10RF Control, Write a code record: saves the code record buffer as the record of the last code received.

standardCommands.name: readCodeRecord
standardCommands.description: EZX10RF Control, Read a code record: loads the record of the last code received into the code record buffer.

standardCommands.name: getCodeRecord
standardCommands.description: EZX10RF Control, Get a code record: has the device send the code record buffer, for the last code received, in an extended message.

standardCommands.name: requestCodeRecord
standardCommands.description: Specific Code Record Read: asks for a record. The device answers with an extended Code record request Response (cmd1 0xF1, cmd2 the record), D1 through D8 the record.

notes: An Insteon group command is sent for an X10 address whose record is in use and linked; a broadcast for one whose record is only in use. The broadcast (Status Change, cmd1 0x27) carries the record number, 0x00 through 0x13, in cmd2 bits 0 to 5, and the X10 command in bits 6 and 7: 00 Off, 01 Dim, 10 On, 11 Bright.

Code records: the device keeps a record for each code it has learned, 20 in all (0x00 through 0x13), and works on one at a time in the code record buffer. Specific Code Record Write (extended, cmd1 0xF2, cmd2 the record) writes D1 through D8 to a record. A record's 8 bytes: flags (bit 7 in use, bit 6 has an Insteon link, bits 0 to 4 the timer), the X10 house and unit code, the X10 command (not used), the Insteon group (1 to 20), then cmd1 and cmd2 sent when the signal turns on and cmd1 and cmd2 sent when it turns off.

The EZX10RF Insteon Messages/Commands give the record's timer in 0.5-second steps; the Quick-Start Guide EZX10RF Wireless Sensor Receiver adds half a minute for each tap of the SET button, for 0.5 to 15.5 minutes.

Peek and Poke addresses, with Set Address MSB 0x00: 0x00 the last X10 house and unit code received (r), 0x01 the last X10 command received (r), 0x02 firmware revision (r), 0x03 EEPROM loaded (r), 0x04 to 0x23 the X10 address filter, 16 by 16 bits, 0x24 to 0x2B the code record buffer (rw). The document gives these addresses without a prefix, as 04-35 and 36-43; read as decimal, they match the filter's 32 bytes and the buffer's 8.
The device answers an ID Request with an acknowledgment and a SET Button Pressed broadcast, without entering linking mode.
Its Poke description says to follow a Poke with Load EEPROM from RAM, which its command table doesn't list.
sources: Quick-Start Guide EZX10RF Wireless Sensor Receiver
